row.team_price_text: Enterprise Self-hosted: $63.60/vCPU core/yr, minimum 250 cores ($15,900/yr) plus $2,120 one-time setup
row.evidence: IBM Kubecost's user-management docs cover only SAML 2.0 and OIDC sign-in with RBAC ("SSO and RBAC are Kubecost Enterprise only features"); no SCIM endpoint or user-provisioning API is documented on the pricing page, docs or API directory.
row.notes: Status unchanged (none). Now sold as IBM Kubecost: Foundations (always free, unlimited users, up to 250 cores), Enterprise Self-hosted (IBM Store: $63.60 per virtual processor core per year, minimum 250 cores = $15,900/yr, plus $2,120 one-time setup) and Enterprise Cloud (Contact Us). Team plan changed from Free to Enterprise Self-hosted because the brief defines team_plan as the cheapest paid tier; Foundations already allows unlimited users. Per-core pricing, so per-user fields are null. The June "Business ~$449/mo" tier no longer appears on any first-party page and was dropped. Access is controlled by SAML/OIDC assertions and group-to-role filters; Kubecost has no SCIM or user API.

scim.notes: No SCIM documented; access comes from SAML/OIDC assertions with group-based RBAC. Absence inferred from the docs TOC, user-management pages and API directory.

roles.how: SAML/OIDC group assertions mapped to admin, readonly, editor roles and custom filters.json access roles (not SCIM)

user_api.notes: The Kubecost API directory covers cost monitoring, governance, diagnostics and savings APIs only; no user endpoints.

okta.notes: Okta SAML set up as a custom app per IBM docs; https://www.okta.com/integrations/kubecost/ returns 404.

entra.notes: Entra SAML/OIDC guides in IBM docs; no Kubecost entry in the Entra SaaS tutorial TOC.

fallbacks.notes: Users are not provisioned at all: SAML/OIDC sign-in grants access and roles from assertions, so there is no separate account lifecycle.

open_questions: Whether Enterprise Cloud (SaaS) offers any user provisioning beyond "Bring your own identity provider".
Whether SAML sign-in creates a persistent user record (JIT) or only a session; docs describe role assignment from assertions only.
